agent_vs_you: The agent's decomposition was right: a qwen-lettered title card, a text-to-video lake shot, then assemble. It also stated the timing plainly in extra ('Hold title_card.png from 0 to 2 seconds; hard cut to sunrise_lake.mp4 from 2 to 6 seconds'). assemble.js reads no per-piece timing from extra. With seconds 6 and two pieces it gives each piece share = 6/2 = 3 s, so the picture got 3 s and the 4.46 s lake clip was cut to 3 s. The cut landed at 3.02 s. The catalogue promises assemble 'GUARANTEES the exact order, the exact length' but never says how the length is divided, so the agent had no reason to expect its timing to be dropped. I would get exact 2 s + 4 s from the current tools by making each piece its own length first: assemble the title alone for 2 s, trim the lake clip to 0–4 s, then assemble the two clips with seconds 0, which keeps clips at their own length. That only works if you know assemble's undocumented even split. The real defect is the harness silently ignoring stated timing.

your_plan.say: I'll make the cream-on-dark-green title card and a slow misty sunrise lake shot, hold the title for exactly 2 seconds, cut to 4 seconds of the lake, and keep it silent.

params.prompt_or_change: Minimalist title card: solid flat dark green background (#1F3D2B) with exactly "A quieter kind of morning" in elegant cream (#F2E8D0) serif lettering, centred, filling about half the width; no other text, no quotation marks, no decoration.

steps.why: Designed title lettering runs on qwen and is read back. This was already correct in the agent's run.

params.prompt_or_change: Hold the title card for exactly 2 seconds.

steps.why: With one picture, assemble gives it the whole 'seconds': exactly 2.0 s (60 frames) plus a silent track.

params.prompt_or_change: Cinematic misty mountain lake at sunrise: low mist drifting over still water, soft golden light touching the peaks and their reflections, a very slow, gentle push forward; no people, no text.

steps.why: A free scene suits text-to-video. minimax returns about 4.46 s, and the harness drops its invented audio.
Gives the lake shot its exact 4.0 s by code.

params.prompt_or_change: Title first, then a hard cut to the lake; silent.

steps.why: seconds 0 keeps each clip at its own length (2.0 + 4.0 = 6.0 s) with a hard cut at 2.0 s. No music input, so it stays silent.

fix: assemble.js: honour per-piece durations, via extra 'durations: 2, 4' or the 'from X to Y' wording planners already write, and let them override the even split. When the total is set and only some pieces have durations, give clips their own length and pictures the remainder rather than share = T/n. If a stated timing cannot be parsed, fail loudly instead of splitting evenly. Add to the catalogue line: 'per-piece seconds in extra (durations: 2, 4); otherwise pictures share what the clips leave'.
evidence: quieter_morning.mp4 is 1280x720, 6.02 s, with a silent audio track. Scene detection finds the only cut at 3.02 s. A 2 fps grid shows the title card in the first 6 frames (0–2.5 s), cream serif 'A quieter kind of morning' on flat dark green, correct and legible, then a misty sunrise lake with drifting mist. title_card.png is 626x352; sunrise_lake.mp4 is 4.46 s, video only. assemble.js computes share = T / vis.length, so each piece gets 3 s, and parses no timing from extra. The judge's only failure (title still on screen at 2.3 s, lake from 3.8 s) is accurate, so the grader is right.
